explanation.correct_game: The rulebook describes a card game of selling piles of identical goods cards for points (hand management, action cards, scoring table). The sheet describes a different game: announcing visible apples and breads, challenging with "Y a un pépin !", and collecting cards as penalties (fewest cards wins). Same name, completely different rules.
explanation.major_errors:
WRONG Shuffle all cards (goods cards and action cards together) to form a single common draw pile in the center of the table. -> Sheet: "Mélangez les cartes de base vertes et formez une pioche face cachée" after removing the green base cards, and special cards are optional additions, not all shuffled together as in the rulebook.
WRONG On your turn you chain two or three simple actions chosen among: draw, lay down, sell. -> Sheet: turn is flip a card, announce, and challenge, not 2-3 actions among draw/lay down/sell.
WRONG Draw: take one card from the central draw pile to add to your hand. -> Sheet has the player draw the top card and place it face up on a central pile, not add it to their hand.
WRONG Action cards can be drawn during the game and let a player steal a card from a neighbor, force someone to sell immediately, or swap hands with another player. -> Sheet's special cards (purple/blue, pain grillé, etc.) have announcement effects; none steal, force a sale, or swap hands.
WRONG Points come only from sold piles; each pile is worth points according to the number of identical cards in it at the time of sale. -> Sheet: "Chaque carte ramassée compte un point de malus", whereas the rulebook scores points from sold piles by number of identical cards.
WRONG The player with the highest total of points from sold piles wins. -> Sheet: "Le joueur qui a ramassé le moins de cartes gagne la partie", not the highest total of points.

explanation.correct_game: The rulebook describes a card-selling game: hand management, sale piles, a points table and action cards. The sheet describes a different game, a real-time announcing game with Pommes, Pains, Pommes de pin and penalty cards, where the fewest cards wins. Only the title matches.
explanation.major_errors:
WRONG Shuffle all cards (goods cards and action cards together) to form a single common draw pile in the center of the table. -> Sheet says "Ne gardez que les cartes de base vertes" and forms a face-down draw pile. Special cards are optional and set aside, so goods and action cards are not shuffled together.
WRONG On your turn you chain two or three simple actions chosen among: draw, lay down, sell. -> Sheet says a turn is to flip a card and announce the visible Pommes and Pains, not to chain two or three actions among draw, lay down and sell.
WRONG Draw: take one card from the central draw pile to add to your hand. -> Sheet has the player flip a card from the draw pile and place it face up. It is not added to the hand.
WRONG Lay down: place one or more cards of the same type in front of you to start or add to a pile. -> The sheet describes three starting piles of face-up cards with a fixed pile order, not laying down cards of the same type from hand.
WRONG Action cards can be drawn during the game and let a player steal a card from a neighbor, force someone to sell immediately, or swap hands with another player. -> The sheet's optional special cards (Pain perdu, Pain rassi, Tarte tatin, etc.) are physical or announcement effects. None steals a card, forces a sale or swaps hands.
WRONG The game ends as soon as the draw pile is empty and nobody can draw any more. -> Sheet says the game ends when a player flips the last card of the draw pile and makes the announcement, not when the pile is empty and nobody can draw.
WRONG Points come only from sold piles; each pile is worth points according to the number of identical cards in it at the time of sale. -> Sheet scores by counting penalty cards collected in front of you, not points from sold piles.
WRONG The player with the highest total of points from sold piles wins. -> Sheet says "Le joueur qui a le moins de cartes remporte la partie", whereas the rulebook says the highest points total from sold piles wins.
WRONG In case of a tie, the tied player with the fewest cards left in hand wins. -> Sheet says several players can win together and gives no tie-break. The rulebook breaks ties by fewest cards left in hand.
